nodes.label: SvelteKit HTML Shell
nodes.rationale: Single static shell with %sveltekit.head%/%sveltekit.body% placeholders and hover preloading; it is the only HTML document because the app is a client-rendered SPA packaged by adapter-static.

nodes.label: Filter Kind Extension Point
nodes.rationale: A new filter kind is one file in filters/kind/ plus two lines in filter.ts, plus one editor file and one else-if branch. Mirrors src-tauri/src/filters/ so both sides grow the same way.

nodes.label: Slice Two Measurement Caches
nodes.rationale: Results are cached as in-memory impacts and persisted stats/statsKey, both keyed by chainKey(effectiveChain(slice)); anything showing a case count must compare that key or an edited chain leaves stale numbers on screen.

nodes.label: Request/Response Type Prefix Convention
nodes.rationale: Types at a call boundary carry a direction prefix (Response*/Request*) so the prefix marks what an invoker hands over directly; nested types stay unprefixed.

nodes.label: Base Slice
nodes.rationale: The one Slice per Project whose chain prefixes every other Slice's chain, the shared cleanup before comparison. Created lazily so an unfiltered Project has no Slice rows at all.

nodes.label: Column Mapping
nodes.rationale: Correspondence between raw file columns and the fields process mining requires (case ID, activity, timestamp). Captured once at project creation; every column appears in it, meaningless ones carry role 'other'.

nodes.label: Distribution
nodes.rationale: Counts of one attribute's values over a node's events split by Group. Describes a shape rather than comparing Groups, so it carries no p-value and no Effect Direction.

nodes.label: Distribution Scope
nodes.rationale: Which of a node's cases' events are counted: 'At this step' vs 'Whole case'. The case set is identical either way; only which events count changes. Not called Variant scope because a non-leaf node sits on many Variants.

nodes.label: Event Log
nodes.rationale: The parsed, typed table for a Project, persisted as Parquet after mapping is confirmed. One per Project, never re-derived from the raw upload.

nodes.label: Filter
nodes.rationale: An event-level predicate lifted to whole cases, its mode picking the lift (mandatory/forbidden/keep_selected/trim). Stored as a definition and re-evaluated on demand, never materialized, so filtering is non-destructive.

nodes.label: Hidden Column
nodes.rationale: Excluded from all analysis, not merely from display: inert until un-hidden. Distinct from a column that is simply not shown.

nodes.label: Local-First Process Mining App
nodes.rationale: A Tauri desktop app where users upload event logs and the app derives process maps, variants, statistics and a data table. All data stays on-device.

nodes.label: Population
nodes.rationale: A set of cases the Statistics view puts in one column. The whole log is a Population but not a Slice: it has no chain and is never stored.

nodes.label: Project
nodes.rationale: A user-created workspace wrapping one uploaded event log plus its metadata and parsed data. Named Project rather than Workspace or analysis to avoid competing vocabulary.

nodes.label: Project Draft
nodes.rationale: A chosen upload whose Column Mapping is not yet confirmed. Has no Project and no Event Log, so abandoning the flow leaves nothing behind.

nodes.label: Slice
nodes.rationale: A named, ordered AND-chain of Filters and the population it produces. Order is user-visible and matters because each Filter applies to the previous one's output. Slices are the unit compared against each other.

nodes.label: Structured-Params IPC Boundary
nodes.rationale: Structured params in, computed results out; never a raw SQL/query string across IPC, because Polars calls are Rust method chains rather than a string query language.

nodes.label: Hidden Columns Enforced by Query-Time Metadata Flag
nodes.norm_label: hidden columns enforced by query-time metadata flag
nodes.rationale: Hidden columns stay in the Parquet file and are filtered by a metadata flag read at query time, so un-hiding never requires re-parsing.

nodes.label: directed_tree Single-Payload Build
nodes.rationale: Ships every Node Aggregate, Significance Test and Co-movement pair in one payload precisely so the frontend never re-aggregates. Distributions are the deliberate exception.

nodes.label: node_distributions Command
nodes.rationale: Keyed on the node's leaf Variant keys and its depth rather than an activity prefix, so node identity is never re-derived from labels on either side. The drawer refuses to fetch while the tree is stale because those keys come from the tree on screen.

nodes.label: Domain-Oriented Frontend Architecture
nodes.rationale: src/lib is organized by what a file is about, not what it is. Six domains each own components, state, invokers, contracts, utilities and tests, so reading one feature means opening one directory instead of five.

nodes.label: CLI-Managed shadcn UI Directory
nodes.rationale: src/lib/components/ui/ is treated as generated: never hand-edited, re-run the shadcn-svelte add/update CLI instead. $lib/utils.ts and $lib/hooks/ stay put because components.json pins those aliases.

nodes.label: One Invoker File Per Tauri Command
nodes.norm_label: one invoker file per tauri command
nodes.rationale: Each Tauri command gets one file in <domain>/invokers/ named after it, so invoker -> contract -> Rust command is one-to-one; components call the invoker rather than invoke() directly.

nodes.label: Deep Imports, No Barrel Files
nodes.rationale: Importing from the exact module path rather than a domain index keeps every dependency visible in the import line.

nodes.label: One-Way Domain Dependency Rule
nodes.rationale: statistics | tree | distributions -> slices -> filters -> event-log, plus distributions -> tree. Nothing points back up, so a dependency cycle cannot form and each domain can be read bottom-up.

nodes.label: SPA Mode (no SSR)
nodes.rationale: Tauri has no Node server, so +layout.ts sets ssr = false and adapter-static uses fallback index.html; the whole app is client-rendered and routes resolve in the browser after load.

nodes.label: Thin Routes Convention
nodes.rationale: Routes handle URL structure and page composition only. Four routes (distributions, new, filters, tree) are still fat and are a known deferred cleanup.

nodes.label: ADR 0001: Split Metadata and Analytics Backends
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: split metadata and analytics backends
nodes.rationale: Metadata stays in sqlite queried from TS via plugin-sql + Drizzle; parsing, Parquet conversion and Polars analytics live in Rust behind tauri::commands. All-Rust and all-TS were rejected: no duckdb/Polars equivalent on the webview side, no Python runtime for pandas, and the developer is not yet fluent in Rust, so only the part that genuinely needs Rust is written in it.

nodes.label: ADR 0002: Persist Parsed Parquet, Keep Raw Original
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002: persist parsed parquet, keep raw original
nodes.rationale: The mapped log is written once as typed Parquet at {app_data}/projects/{id}/event_log.parquet and is the working copy. Re-parsing on every cold load was rejected as repeated cost for no benefit; deleting the raw upload was rejected because it forecloses re-running column mapping and removes a fallback against a future conversion bug.

nodes.label: ADR 0003: Query Distributions On Demand
nodes.rationale: Distributions are fetched per selected node by node_distributions rather than shipped with directed_tree, because they are offered for every non-hidden column under two Scopes; build-time computation would multiply the most expensive operation by column count and Scope to produce numbers read one node at a time.

nodes.label: ADR 0004: Domain-Oriented Frontend Architecture
nodes.rationale: Reorganized src/lib from by-kind to by-domain because reading one feature meant opening five directories and components/projects/ had grown to 35 files covering every feature. Each domain maps to a module under src-tauri/src/ and four map to a route, so a URL names the directory that serves it.

nodes.label: Deferred Filter Editor Split and Fat Route Thinning
nodes.norm_label: deferred filter editor split and fat route thinning
nodes.rationale: Splitting filter-editor.svelte (833 lines, ~18 shared $state variables) into per-kind editors and thinning the four fat routes are rewrites rather than moves, so they belong in their own reviews.

nodes.label: End-to-End Tests Blocked on macOS
nodes.rationale: tauri-driver supports Linux and Windows only, so Playwright cannot drive the real Tauri window on macOS, and browser testing would mean mocking invoke() and plugin-sql wholesale. Blocked rather than deferred.

nodes.label: Project and Event Log Are One Domain
nodes.norm_label: project and event log are one domain
nodes.rationale: Project.columns is ColumnMapping[] and createProject calls addProject, so splitting them would create bidirectional references; event_log/commands.rs already treats them as one module.

nodes.label: db/schema.ts Stays One File
nodes.rationale: Deliberate exception to domain ownership: seeing every table in one place beats strict ownership, so schema.ts imports persisted types from four domains.

nodes.label: statistics/ Stays Its Own Domain
nodes.rationale: Owns no state and no types and takes every input from slices/, but keeping directories mapped one-to-one to routes makes navigation predictable.

nodes.label: Pass Icons as Components, Not String Keys
nodes.norm_label: pass icons as components, not string keys
